reviewScope: Independent technical pre-incorporation review of the unsigned R8-corrected round-two remediation candidate against the exact canonical target, accepted Gate 1 record, frozen round-two evidence, and preserved Critic records R1 through R8. The review independently verified all 50 manifest hashes and exact canonical Exam bytes, ran full and fixtures-only validators, reproduced every declared R8 provider-receipt and replay case, independently probed one-to-one provider receipt cardinality, order, tuple, provider, version, key, request, idempotency, proof and temporal binding, confirmed exact committed same-byte replay and crash-cut convergence, confirmed the R3 through R7 closures and full matrix execution, and treated authorized App incorporation as a governed next state rather than a pre-incorporation defect.

integrityChecks.validatorReported: PASS R8 corrected candidate oracles only; next state is fresh-context preflight, not canonicalization

decision.rationale: The 50-file package is hash-consistent, both validator modes pass, every declared matrix row and coverage kind executes, exact committed same-byte replay converges deleted-tombstoned with lifecycle effect zero, crash-cut recovery converges as declared, and provider receipt cardinality, proof corruption, status, time, order, tuple, request, resource, key and aggregate mismatches fail with typed zero effects. One blocker remains: the provider receipt verifier does not establish an independent provider trust domain. Provider receipts are signed with the same embedded private key used by the ordinary local candidate signer, and the provider-specific key ID is rewritten after signing and derived from the receipt's self-asserted provider. An ordinary local signer can therefore mint novel receipts that verify as provider-authentic and drive deleted-tombstoned. Zero technical blocker or major is not met, so the candidate is not ready for authorized incorporation.

newFindings.title: Provider receipt signatures are not anchored to an independent provider trust domain

observedCase.construction: Start from the valid two-copy RC-FAILED-RUN fixture. For each provider receipt, replace providerReceiptId, providerRequestId and providerTransactionId with novel values, remove recordDigest and signature, sign the resulting receipt preimage with the exported ordinary local sealRecord signer, and then rewrite only the excluded signature.keyId metadata to provider:<self-asserted-provider>:fixture-ed25519-rfc8032-1. Coherently refresh the aggregate receipt, tombstone and final immutable commit request. No independent provider key or trust-store evidence is used.
observedCase.expected: Block with typed zero effects because a locally generated signature must not be accepted as independent provider proof of a destructive effect.
observedCase.observed: lifecycleDecision returned deleted-tombstoned with firstError null and effects.lifecycle=1 for two novel locally minted provider receipts. The ordinary local signer and provider receipt signer share the same seed, private key and public key; changing the unsigned keyId metadata was sufficient to enter the provider verification path.

newFindings.impact: A lifecycle worker, compromised local evidence signer, or any component holding the candidate-local signing capability can fabricate provider receipt, request and transaction identities and obtain a durable deletion or crypto-erasure tombstone without an independently authenticated provider effect. The R8 fix therefore still cannot distinguish provider evidence from locally manufactured evidence.
newFindings.requiredResolution: Create explicit signer-domain separation. Define a hash-bound provider trust store or independently archived provider-key evidence keyed by exact provider identity and validity interval. Verify each provider receipt against the trusted public key selected from that external binding, not against a publicKeyHex or keyId supplied by or derived only from the receipt. Use provider-specific fixture private keys distinct from every local record signer, keep private keys out of the verifier, and bind provider identity, trust-store entry/version, key ID, proof authority and receipt preimage under the signature. Add executable negatives in which the ordinary local signer, another provider's valid signer, a self-asserted provider/key ID, an untrusted rotated key, and an out-of-validity key sign otherwise coherent receipts; each must block with typed zero effects. Add a positive provider-key rotation case and preserve all current provider receipt, one-to-one and replay cases. Refresh all affected hashes and repeat fresh independent pre-incorporation review.
